sam-eng: Hey support — seeing intermittent 429s and weird token billing spikes when we do regen + parallel embeddings prefetch across two models (rwd3-long / rwd3-compact). Happens only under bursty user load. No 401s.

sam-eng: Example: we kick off a regen and in parallel prefetch embeddings for 8 items. ~200ms after the regen start we see a flurry of 429s. SDK v0.9.3.

sam-eng: curl snippet we used:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd3-long","prompt":"...","max_tokens":512}'
```

sam-eng: then in parallel we call embeddings for 8 docs across rwd3-compact. Token billing for those regen requests looks doubled (billing shows regen tokens + embed tokens, not sure if double-count).

alex-support: sorry about the trouble — can you confirm if calls are fanout from a single request (server does parallel calls per user request) or coming as separate client requests? Also, can you paste the X-RateLimit and Retry-After headers if present?

sam-eng: fanout from server: yes, our backend spawns 8 concurrent embed requests when a user uploads a doc and triggers regen. We grabbed a sample response header when it happened:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Model: 1200/tpm
X-RateLimit-Model-Remaining: 0
Retry-After: 3
```

sam-eng: header shows per-model limit being hit. But we called two different model ids (rwd3-long + rwd3-compact). Why would compact limit show up for regen on rwd3-long?

maria-ml: quick note — our platform enforces per-model TPM and a separate max concurrency per model variant. If you do high fanout from one process across variants, you can hit per-model TPM for each variant; also, internal routing may map rwd3-long regen to a compatible variant when rwd3-long capacity is constrained which can surface the other model's headers.

maria-ml: also check if your server reuses the same API key for both requests. TPM quotas are keyed by API key + model. If you have a single API key doing both, you'll see per-model exhaustion behavior across calls.

sam-eng: we are reusing one key (same service account). Good catch. Is there a way to see per-key per-model windows to prove this?

alex-support: we can pull your recent rate header traces. Meanwhile, short-term mitigations:
- add jittered backoff on embed prefetch (exponential with jitter)
- reduce concurrent embed fanout (batch embeddings where possible)
- pin regen to a lower-context variant if you can (rwd3-compact) or avoid long max_tokens during heavy fanout
- if you need guaranteed throughput, consider Dedicated capacity / reserved pool for that model to avoid shared TPM throttles

ops-bot: @sam-eng we found traces for api key ending ***abcd. There are repeated bursts where 8 parallel embed calls + regen request exceed model TPM for rwd3-compact at minute 2905001100. See trace id: trace-2905-01.

sam-eng: thanks. Any explanation on the billing/token double-count we saw? Looks like regen tokens + embed tokens are both counted (expected) but we saw sums higher than we measured on client side.

jeff-platform: billing note from infra — when you do concurrent requests that include overlapping context (e.g., you send the same long conversation to regen and to an embed prefetch that includes the conversation), there can be transient duplicate token accounting before server-side prefix caching dedupes. It's rare but visible under bursts. We can check your traces for cache hits/misses.

sam-eng: repro steps I can share: locally run this script that fires one regen and N parallel embed calls (N=8) with same API key, with regen max_tokens=512, embed batch size 1. On our prod-like env we reproduce ~40% of attempts producing 429s and a few with higher billed tokens.

sam-eng: also seeing slightly higher latency (p50->p95 jump) for regen when embed fanout occurs.

maria-ml: sounds consistent with hitting per-model concurrency/TPM limits and also causing queueing which spikes latency. If you want we can:
- inspect the traces for the exact model variant routing (to see if regen was rerouted to compact)
- provide a per-minute breakdown of model TPM consumption for your key

alex-support: created an internal ticket SUP-2905-embed-fanout. We'll pull the trace data and share recommended throttle headers and a suggested client-side concurrency limit.

sam-eng: much appreciated. One more question: we saw Retry-After: 3 but still got a burst of 429s for ~10s after. Is there a burst window we should be aware of?

maria-ml: there is a short burst smoothing window; when a model's TPM is exceeded, queued requests may be rejected until tokens are replenished. Retry-After is approximate — we suggest exponential backoff with randomized jitter starting at Retry-After and doubling. Also consider spreading prefetch across a short time window (50-200ms) to avoid synchronized bursts.

alex-support: closing the loop: we'll attach traces to SUP-2905 and send a follow-up with precise per-model TPM numbers and a recommended concurrency cap for your workload. If you'd like, we can simulate a suggested cap in a staging trace to show expected reduction in 429s.

sam-eng: great. Please reopen if you need sample logs from our side. We'll try batching and add jitter for now. Thanks! :thumbsup:
